terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: An enclosed vendor cart on two open bicycle wheels and two swivel casters. The bicycle wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Both doors are part of the cabinet shell at two draw calls, and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. Every soi mouth at dusk. Rusting silver frame, dark slate panels, a stainless top worn to brushed grey, an oval broth well with a ladle, open chrome bicycle wheels on one end and casters on the other.

reasoning: TWO merges and ONE InstancedMesh: THREE draw calls of 4. The PAINT merge is the dark sheet body, four framed elevations as extrusions with a real opening cut in each, a pierced deck, two door leaves with mouldings, pulls and strap hinges, the rust hem, reveal creep, corner blooms and hinge bleeds, the axle and two swivel casters. The STEEL merge is the two-plate counter with the basin cut out of it, the oval basin, the broth, the ladle bowl and handle, and the two push-handle tubes with their ferrules. The InstancedMesh is the two open bicycle wheels.

TWO materials of the three allowed, because one roughness cannot be both halves of this prop: paint at 0.80/0.03 for chalky worn sheet and steel at 0.34/0.55 for brushed stainless with real highlights. At a single 0.52/0.22 the counter read as another painted panel. Both are WHITE with every tone a vertex colour -- frame #9c948a, door leaf #a2a096 (the plate reads the leaves lighter than the frame, its clean door #9c9a94 at luma 155), panel #53686e, counter #a4a29b, well #a8a49a, broth #a4835b, rust #7a6248, stain #8f8371, tyre #3d3d3a, rim #c6c6c1. The registry description's "glazed side panel" is the plate's dark painted panel; no transparent state is needed.
One repetition system: two open bicycle wheels off one geometry of two ring lathes, twelve prism spokes, a hub and a dome cap, each a named pivot.
Action readiness: two hinge pivots on the bicycle wheels, one box collider, zero sockets, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is a near-cubic dark cabinet in a broad worn frame under a stainless counter almost filled by an oval broth basin, on two open bicycle wheels; a well that does not fill its counter reads as a pot lid on a table, and closed wheel discs read as a cupboard on castors.

resolvedUnknowns: The panels are painted sheet, not glass: the plate shows opaque dark slate; the description's glazed panel is not built.
Both bicycle wheels are on the -X end with the axle along Z, so the cart is pushed along X by the handles.

The panel is authored on CHROMA, not luma, and ships MORE saturated than the plate. The turntable gate calls a pixel background when it is within 24 of #3a3a3a AND at saturation <= 0.16; at a near-neutral #5b6260 the end elevations rendered #343a38 and #3b413f -- distance 5.7 and 9.1, saturation 0.10 -- and 38,612 px of solid panel was read as a hole punched through the cart at azimuth 90 and 270. Lifting to grey would need an authored luma of 134 (the render returns 0.58 of it), which is nothing like the plate. The plate's panel IS cool -- #2f3333 shaded and #737d7e lit, green and blue 4-11 levels over red in both -- so the same cast is pushed to #53686e at saturation 0.245 and luma 100. That drops the enclosed-background count at azimuth 90 from 38,612 px to 1,059 -- the handle loops alone. A near-neutral lift would have needed an authored luma of 143 to clear the distance test, which is the frame's own value and would erase the panel; a stronger #486661 passed too but rendered as a green teal nothing like the plate. Saturation 0.245 against the plate's measured 0.06-0.08 is the price of the pass, and it is what caps the material layer.

The basin is an OVAL, not a circle. Solving the rim ellipse's screen extents on the plate (283..670 px across, 215..340 px down) against the counter's projected plan vectors gives r/L 0.393 and r/D 0.456 -- 79% of the counter's length and 91% of its depth -- which a single revolution cannot be, so the lathe is revolved at the depth radius and stretched 1.35 along x.
The -Z long elevation and the +X end are NOT observed. Both are built as the mirror of what is: two openings on the long face, one on the end. Confidence 0.85.
The declared depth was corrected 0.75 -> 0.88 before building, on the proxy's 0.871.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.50 x 1.50 x 0.88 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 2 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: A 1.06 x 0.945 x 0.76 m cabinet from 0.20 to 1.145 m under a 1.096 x 0.796 x 0.060 counter; an oval basin 0.864 x 0.640 at the rim sunk to 1.026 with broth at 1.116 and a ladle rising to 1.500; horizontal U handles at y 1.09 reaching +-0.745; two open r 0.175 wheels at x -0.455, z +-0.405; two r 0.052 casters at x +0.462, z +-0.26.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: Built 1.520 x 1.508 x 0.884: x +-0.760 at the push handles (declared 1.50), y 0 to 1.508 at the ladle handle (declared 1.50), z +-0.442 at the bicycle wheels (declared 0.88, corrected from 0.75 on the proxy). The proxy, banded in metres at the declared 1.50 m height, is the whole station list: cabinet x -0.556..0.502 and z -0.393..0.370 over y 0.20..1.20, the dense 1.15-1.20 band its counter slab; the x +-0.745 lobes at y 1.05-1.15 its handles; r 0.175 wheels at x -0.455 and z +-0.405; casters at x +0.50; and above 1.20 the ladle alone. The FIRST build read those as a cabinet 0.30-0.98 by 0.66 deep on r 0.27 wheels -- a squat long box under two giant discs -- and that single misreading is most of its 0.84.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1:1.000:0.581, banded in metres at the declared height it gives every station above. Its ladle sits at x -0.22, z -0.40 above 1.20 -- a fused stick whose lean is noisy -- so the ladle angle is read off the plate and the rest off the proxy.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.85: the back is a second dark panel in the same frame; the door is on the front only.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Counter 1.096 x 0.796 as TWO stacked pierced plates, 1.145-1.192 at full plan and 1.192-1.205 inset 10 mm, for the bullnosed edge the plate shows; a pressed groove 30 mm in and three scoring lines; oval basin 0.864 x 0.640 at the rim with its floor at 1.026 and broth at 1.116; ladle bowl 0.180 x 0.072 with its handle to 1.500; U handles r 0.014 at y 1.090 reaching +-0.745 with ferrules at the end frames.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The basin passes through the counter as an interpenetrating solid and its rim rolls over and tucks back UNDER the counter top at 1.199, below the top face at 1.205, so no shell backside faces the camera and the opening cut wall stays buried in the basin collar all the way to the soffit. The counter overhangs the cabinet, an opposed joint. check-coplanar is clean at 0.001 m.

evidence: Measured on the plate: clean door #9c9a94 sd 13 luma 155 and worn frame 134-218; panel lit #737d7e luma 123 against shaded #2f3333 luma 50; counter 139-184; well #9f998e / #a79986; broth #a4835b sat 0.45; caster #49443d. Carried as vertex colours on a WHITE material: frame #9c948a, door leaf #aaa79d, panel #5b6260, counter #a4a29b, well #a8a49a, broth #a4835b, rim #c6c6c1, hub #9a9a95, tyre #4a4a47 (luma 74), rust #7a6248, stain #8f8371.

Textureless as DECLARED: a 512 px grime canvas after construction, height-keyed at 1.7 m so a single pass covers the whole prop -- at 0.8 m its ground wash repeated at y 0.8 and drew a hard tide line across the door.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 3,800/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/8 unique geometries, two grime canvases. Turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement, covering ONLY what is genuinely open -- the two handle loops, the wheels between rim and hub, and a thin arc of the basin inner wall -- painted with holeviz to confirm the panel is no longer classified at any azimuth.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components and one repetition system: 3 of 4.

materials.note: paint and steel: 2 of 3; every tone within each is a vertex colour.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,800 of 4,000: seventy-odd boxes, seven extrusions (four pierced elevations, a pierced deck and two pierced counter plates), one 28-segment stretched lathe, an ellipsoid, thirteen cylinders, three tubes, and one open wheel instanced twice.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Extrusions with holes for the framed elevations, the deck and the counter; boxes for the body, doors, hardware and wear; a stretched lathe for the basin; an ellipsoid for the ladle bowl; tubes for the handles and the ladle; ring lathes, prism spokes and cylinders for the wheels and casters.
One InstancedMesh: two open bicycle wheels, each a named pivot with its instance index.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two grime canvases after construction -- 512 px ochre on the paint, 256 px light on the steel -- 0.33 MB, the factory built in 136 ms.

risks.description: The plate's panel is a near-neutral dark slate, and the turntable gate read 38,612 px of it as background at azimuth 90 and 270 -- a hole through the cart, not a dark surface.
risks.mitigation: Authored on chroma at #53686e, saturation 0.245, which clears the gate's 0.16 ceiling at every azimuth. --allow-holes then covers only what is genuinely open: the two handle loops, the wheels between rim and hub, and a thin arc of the basin's shaded inner wall, all confirmed on the _holecc measurement and painted with holeviz.

risks.description: The wheels are genuinely open between rim and hub, so the turntable gate reads the gaps between the spokes as background punched through the model.
risks.mitigation: --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement, exactly as the som-tam cart's bicycle wheels. It was NOT used to get past the panel failure above: that was fixed in the albedo first, and holeviz confirms the panel is no longer classified at any azimuth.

risks.description: The basin reaches down to 1.026 and a body box carried to the counter put its own top face across the inside of the bowl, rendering as a flat dark disc where the broth should be.
risks.mitigation: The body stops at 1.100 and a pierced deck carries on to the counter soffit, its opening tighter than the counter's so the basin wall closes both.

risks.description: An earlier build put the wheel discs across Z (rz) and the depth ran to 1.26 m.
risks.mitigation: Corrected to rx: discs in the XY plane on a Z axle.
